name: Jack Emby
role: Intern and film fan — fetches coffee, entertains everyone and gets ready what you'll watch next
bubble.hello_short: Hi, I'm Jack Emby, just the intern here. Mostly I fetch the coffee and keep everyone entertained — oh well.
bubble.loading: One moment, having a quick look…
bubble.intro: Hi, I'm Jack Emby — say it fast and it sounds like "check Emby". With EmbyCache I put what you'll watch next on the fast pool, so the array disks can sleep.
bubble.no_emby: Only: I can't find an Emby container. Without Emby there's nothing for me to do.
bubble.no_python: EmbyCache needs Python 3 for that — the server doesn't have it yet.
bubble.fetch: First I'll fetch EmbyCache from its public repository — one click on "Fetch EmbyCache".
bubble.setup: EmbyCache is here. Now let's set it up: Emby address, API key, libraries and pool.
bubble.running: EmbyCache is running right now — I'm watching.

bubble.on_pool.one: One file ({size}) is ready on the pool.
bubble.on_pool.other: {n} files ({size}) are ready on the pool.

bubble.nothing_yet: Nothing of mine on the pool yet.
bubble.no_schedule: It doesn't run on its own yet — that needs a schedule in User Scripts.

mode_hint.run: Moves what's up next from the array to the pool and brings watched things back. May wake array disks.
tool_sub: The tool I work with — straight from its public repository, nothing in it is changed here.
not_fetched_sub: comes by git clone into data/embycache/app

update_text.other: EmbyCache gets {n} new changes from its public repository. Your settings stay as they are.

overview_sub: The settings in short, the last run and when I start next.
schedule_hint: To run EmbyCache regularly: in Settings → User Scripts add a script named "unraid-secretary-office_embycache" with this content and pick a schedule, e.g. hourly.
on_pool_sub: What EmbyCache put on the pool — as of {when}.
on_pool_none: Nothing yet — after the first real run you'll see here what's ready.
notice.no_emby: No Emby container found. EmbyCache works with an Emby server — you'll find one under Apps.
notice.no_python: Python 3 is missing on the server. Under Apps there is e.g. "Python 3 for UNRAID".
notice.setup: EmbyCache is fetched but not set up yet.
notice.changed: EmbyCache's code was changed here. So I won't update it, to make sure nothing gets lost.
notice.fetch_first: Fetch EmbyCache first — then I can set it up.
help.what_text: EmbyCache asks Emby what you'll watch next (continue watching, next episodes, favourites) and moves those files from the array to the fast pool — under /mnt/user they stay visible in the same place. The array disks may sleep and playback starts right away. Watched things go back to the array.
help.tool_text: A standalone tool by helmi1987. I fetch it from its public repository and update it from there; settings, list and log live separately in data/embycache and survive updates.
help.report: Shows per person what's up next. Changes nothing and wakes no disks.
help.dry: Works out a run and shows what would be moved. Changes nothing.
help.run: Brings watched things back to the array and moves what's up next to the pool. May wake array disks for that.
help.pool_text: So the mover doesn't push the prepared files straight back to the array, EmbyCache's list belongs in Mover Tuning as an exception. The caretaker tells you whether it is.
help.schedule_text: EmbyCache runs regularly through a User Scripts entry. I show you what goes in it.
setup.bubble: Let's set up EmbyCache. First I need your Emby server's address and an API key — with them I ask for libraries and people.
setup.server_sub: Address and API key. The key stays on the server and never comes back to the browser.
setup.name: Name
setup.url_hint: As the Unraid server reaches Emby, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8096
setup.key_hint: In Emby: Settings → Advanced → API Keys → New API Key.
setup.key_kept: saved — leave empty to keep it
setup.libraries_sub: Which libraries EmbyCache looks at — and where their folders are on the server.
setup.map_missing: The server folder for {path} is missing (starts with /mnt/).
setup.users_sub: Who I get things ready for. None selected means: everyone.
setup.scope_sub: Where to and how much. Better start small.
setup.pool_hint: The fast pool EmbyCache moves files to (usually the cache).
setup.mode_count_hint: This many episodes ahead per series.
setup.mode_budget_hint: Whatever fits a fixed budget — shared between films and series.
setup.min_free_hint: Below that EmbyCache moves nothing more to the pool.
setup.next_up_hint: The next episodes of the series people are watching.
setup.save_hint: EmbyCache checks the settings itself before they apply.
setup.help_key: Create a separate API key for EmbyCache in Emby. It is stored on the server (only root can read it) and never sent to the browser.
setup.help_mapping: Emby sees folders from inside its container (e.g. /movies). EmbyCache needs the real paths on the server. I suggest them from the Emby container's settings.
setup.help_scope: Number of episodes is simple and predictable; the budget makes the best use of a fixed amount of space.
setup.help_save: I hand the settings to EmbyCache, which checks them with its own rules and saves them.
fact.setup: EmbyCache is here but not set up yet
check.emby_container_how: Install Emby Server from Apps — otherwise Jack Emby has nothing to do.
check.python_how: Install e.g. "Python 3 for UNRAID" from Apps.
check.configured_how: Jack Emby → "Set up…": address, API key, libraries, pool.
check.schedule_how: Settings → User Scripts: add an entry with embycache_run.py --run and schedule it. Jack Emby shows the content.
check.mover_tuning: The mover leaves prepared files alone
check.mover_tuning_how: Mover Tuning → set "Ignore files listed inside of a text file" to {file}.

errors.emby_local_changes: EmbyCache's code was changed here — I won't update, so nothing gets lost.
errors.emby_bad_url: That's not a valid address (http://… or https://…).
errors.emby_need_key: A valid API key is needed.
errors.emby_bad_key: Emby doesn't accept the API key.
errors.emby_bad_pool: {path} isn't a pool on this server.
fit.yes: Jack Emby is happy to come — he spotted "{name}" and couldn't be stopped.
fit.no_emby: I asked Jack Emby, but as there's no Emby on this server, he didn't want to come.
fire_note: If EmbyCache is scheduled in User Scripts, it keeps running until you switch it off there.
